topics.topic: Whether ordinary record changes end create-replay recognition and what a retry does
questions: Which changes make a created record stop "keeping its values": only erasure or anonymisation that removes its create request id, or also ordinary corrections and lifecycle changes such as archiving, restriction, or ending a relationship; and after such an ordinary change does a retry return the existing record, create another record, or get refused?
Which retained values preserve replay recognition, and do corrections, restriction, relationship changes or archiving end it, or only erasure/anonymisation that removes the stored create request id?
Does changing any value of a Project or Customer by a normal correction end replay recognition for its original create request, or does recognition survive until the record is erased or anonymised?

quotes:
A create whose request id such a record carries is
   a repeat when the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of
   the same kind: Registry answers the record as it stands now and changes
   nothing.

A create whose request id an existing record carries, with facts that
   differ from that record's current ones — a different value, or the record
   corrected since — is refused, and nothing changes; the caller reads the
   record.

A repeat of a project's create after the project was archived answers the
   archived project and does not reactivate it.
A repeat of a project's create after the project was corrected is refused.
judgement.why: State 2 says recognition survives ordinary changes: a correction that changes create facts makes the retry a refusal rather than a new create, while archiving preserves a successful replay and other lifecycle changes do not prevent replay when the supplied create facts still equal the record's current facts.

topics.topic: Whether whole project deletion ends recognition of the original project-create request
questions: Does deleting an archived project whole, rather than anonymising it, also end recognition of its original project-create request and make a later repeat a new create?
Does deleting an archived project whole also make a later repetition of its create request a new create, or is the new exception limited to customer erasure and project anonymisation?
What happens when a project-create request is repeated after the first project was deleted whole rather than anonymised?

quotes:
Registry keeps the request id with the record the create made, written once
   (M01, M03, M04, M05).

A request id is looked up among the records of the same model — for 'add a
   room' and 'publish an artifact pointer', only those of the project the
   call names, so a record of another project is never reached through it.

Kernel's retried 'add a room' or publish and a resubmitted owner form are
safe, and Registry keeps nothing but the request id to tell a repeat.
judgement.why: State 2 keeps replay evidence only on the created record and finds repeats only among existing records, so deleting the Project whole removes the only evidence and the later call is a new create.

topics.topic: Whether the replay exception also covers affected child or related creates such as room creation
questions: Does this rule cover a repeated room create whose Room and request id disappeared when its project was anonymised, or only the create of the Customer or Project that was itself erased or anonymised?

Is this exception limited to repeating the create of the erased Customer or anonymised Project itself, or does it also apply to other create actions whose records or parents were affected, especially room creation?

quotes:
A repeat passes stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 like any call — rights,
   the session's set, the existence of its project, its values, a publish's
   type among them (A22) — and, for 'add a room' and 'publish an artifact
   pointer', the check that its project is not archived (R0-17, R0-88).

Kernel repeating 'add a room' after the project left its session's set is
    answered as not found (A10).
judgement.why: State 2 requires a repeated room create to pass the session-set, project-existence and archived-project checks, so after anonymisation Kernel receives the not-found refusal and no Room is created.

topics.topic: Whether a project create repeated after anonymisation must pass current create preconditions
questions: When a repeated project create is treated as new after anonymisation, must it pass the current create preconditions, or must it always make the promised new record even if its original customer reference is now erased, restricted or ended?

quotes:
A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).

Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session (sign-in
   excepted, A13 rule 4), then for a change its CSRF value (R0-29), then a confirmation value where one is
   asked (A13);
   (2) for agent authority, the session and its set (A10), whose refusal
   hides every later failure; (3) that every record the action names exists —
   its target and any it newly names, such as a customer; (4) the
   values given (A02, A08, A22); (5) the stated revision or access version
   (A12); (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the
   set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict. A transition that passes all six
   may be a repeat that changes nothing (A05). A create's repeat is the one
   exception: it is recognised after stages (1) to (4) and its project's
   archive check (A01 rule 3), and the rest of stage (6) does not apply to
   it.
judgement.why: After anonymisation the call is a new create rather than a recognised repeat, so State 2's sole replay exception does not apply and the restricted customer's eligibility check refuses the request.
